stories.title: Evaluating the accuracy and efficiency of Cloud-to-IDA for drift-based collapse assessment of steel frames under near- and far-field motions
stories.description: Accurate estimation of seismic collapse capacity is essential for performance-based earthquake engineering and fragility assessment. Incremental Dynamic Analysis (IDA) is widely regarded as a reliable benchmark for collapse capacity evaluation; however, its high computational cost limits its application in large-scale or rapid assessment studies. This study evaluates the accuracy and computational efficiency of conventional Cloud Analysis and the Cloud-to-IDA procedure compared with IDA for steel moment-resisting frames subjected to near-field and far-field ground motions and investigates the influence of structural height and ground-motion characteristics on the accuracy of each assessment method. Three two-dimensional steel moment-resisting frames with 3, 5, and 9 stories were modeled in OpenSees and analyzed using 22 far-field and 28 near-field ground motion records from the FEMA P695 suite. Spectral acceleration at the fundamental period, Sa(T1), was adopted as the intensity measure, and maximum inter-story drift ratio was used as the engineering demand parameter. A drift-based collapse limit state was defined using HAZUS inter-story drift thresholds to provide a consistent comparison basis among the three methods. The results show that conventional Cloud Analysis can produce height- and record-dependent bias, with the bias diminishing as frame height increases from 3 to 9 stories, in estimating median collapse capacity. The largest discrepancy was observed for the 3-story frame under far-field records, where Cloud Analysis overestimated the IDA-based median collapse capacity by approximately 20%. In contrast, Cloud-to-IDA closely reproduced the IDA results across all studied frame heights and ground-motion categories, with median collapse capacity errors limited to only a few percent. Dispersion estimates from Cloud-to-IDA were also more consistent with IDA than those obtained from conventional Cloud Analysis. In terms of computational demand, Cloud-to-IDA substantially reduced the number of nonlinear dynamic analyzes and achieved approximately 86–91% reduction in computational time relative to IDA, while maintaining close agreement in both median capacity and dispersion. These findings indicate that Cloud-to-IDA can provide an efficient and reliable alternative for drift-based collapse fragility assessment of steel moment-resisting frames, provided that its applicability is carefully limited to the structural systems, ground-motion sets, and collapse criteria considered in the study.

stories.title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl-carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
stories.description: Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes can mitigate fire risk, but poor bulk and interfacial properties of such electrolytes limit their application. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. The electrolyte comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride, fluoroethylene carbonate, and ethyl methyl carbonate at low concentration establishes a weakly solvating environment, wherein dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride and fluoroethylene carbonate preferentially contribute to stabilize the positive and negative electrodes, while working together to enhance the rate capability, low-temperature performance, and long-term cycling at high-voltage. Accelerating rate calorimetry revealed a delayed thermal runaway onset by 87 °C, correlating with Broadness Index. These findings suggest that preemptive passivation on both electrodes, when coupled with nonflammable electrolyte design, can provide a viable route toward safe, high-energy lithium batteries. Batteries require safe electrolytes without compromising performance. Here, the authors develop a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage, long-lasting, and safe lithium-ion batteries.

stories.title: Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling
stories.description: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform. Kerr parametric oscillators provide a route to protected bosonic quantum states through engineered energy gaps. Here, the authors realize a three-photon Kerr parametric oscillator and demonstrate coherent control of a bosonic qutrit, observing three photon Rabi oscillations, three-component cat states, and an energy gap that suppresses leakage from the qutrit manifold.

stories.title: ARES-SI: adaptive reinforcement-enhanced sampling for suicidal ideation
stories.description: Suicidal ideation (SI) fluctuates rapidly within individuals, but standard ecological momentary assessment (EMA) uses fixed schedules that miss critical risk windows. We present ARES-SI (Adaptive Reinforcement-Enhanced Sampling for Suicidal Ideation), a reinforcement learning system that personalizes EMA timing to individual risk patterns. ARES-SI combines random forest models to predict active SI probability and non-response likelihood with a Q-learning algorithm to determine optimal assessment intervals (30 min for high-risk states, 3 h for low-risk states, and next day to reduce burden). We trained the system using EMA data from 98 participants across three studies with varied sampling frequencies (4–15 assessments per day; 2359 positive active SI responses) over 28-day protocols. In validation testing (N = 34; 374 positive active SI responses), the random forest models achieved an AUC of 0.865 for active SI and 0.750 for non-response. ARES-SI demonstrated 65% higher action selection accuracy than random scheduling (0.781 vs. 0.474; macro F1 = 0.650 vs. 0.377), with stronger detection of high-risk windows (30-min recall = 0.810 vs. 0.392) and efficient low-risk scheduling (3-h precision = 0.972 vs. 0.876). These findings provide initial evidence that reinforcement learning can adapt assessment timing to momentary risk.

stories.title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
stories.description: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance. In this study, the authors benchmark four wastewater sequencing methods for influenza A, including two that were developed in-house. Using a custom probe panel they recover H1N1, H3N2, and H5N1, including H5N1 signals when dPCR was limited.

stories.title: Use of microstream capnography in sedation practices for pediatric patients undergoing magnetic resonance imaging
stories.description: In pediatric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), there is a need for more advanced monitoring methods in addition to routine pulse oximetry to ensure safer nonoperating room anesthesia (NORA). The integrated pulmonary index (IPI) available in the Microstream capnography device provides an early indicator of a patient’s respiratory functions. In this study, we aimed to investigate the feasibility of using the IPI as an early indicator for detecting cardiorespiratory events. A prospective, observational study was conducted on pediatric patients aged 1 month to 18 years who were to undergo sedation for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The respiratory rate (RR), end tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2), oxygen saturation (SpO2), heart rate (HR), complications, and EtCO2 changes (∆EtCO2) were recorded. IPI values at induction and at the end of the scan were evaluated. The primary outcome was the diagnostic performance of the post-induction IPI value in predicting cardiorespiratory events; secondary outcomes included the incidence of cardiorespiratory events and of hypopneic hypoventilation, and the diagnostic performance of EtCO2 for these outcomes. A total of 159 patients were included in the study. ROC analysis revealed the diagnostic significance of EtCO2 induction in predicting hypoxia and apnea. While 31.44% of all patients had ∆EtCO2, only 6.3% of these patients had SpO2 ≤ 93% (hypoxia) at the same time. The induction EtCO2 median in patients who developed hypoxia was 26 mmHg (IQR: 14–29), compared to 33 mmHg (IQR: 28–36) in those without hypoxia (p = 0.001). EtCO2 The optimal threshold value was found to be 29 mmHg in patients who developed hypoxia, whereas it was 18 mmHg in those who developed apnea. A total of 27.7% of all patients had hypopneic hypoventilation, and hypoxia was detected in %15.9 of these patients. IPI, EtCO2, and ∆EtCO2 have a statistically significant effect on ‘induction cardiorespiratory events’. Patients with cardiorespiratory events had an IPI ≤ 6 and EtCO2 ≤ 33. Each one-unit increase in IPI was calculated to reduce the probability of a cardiorespiratory event by approximately 46.3%. Severe respiratory complications are frequently observed in young pediatric patients undergoing NORA. Early diagnosis of respiratory complications, particularly hypopneic hypoventilation, is possible through EtCO2 monitoring. Low EtCO2 and IPI are considered potential risk factors for the development of cardiorespiratory events. The routine use of capnography, a method that allows continuous and noninvasive monitoring of respiration, enhances patient safety in procedural sedation outside the operating room. Intervention in pediatric patients with an IPI value < 6 who develop cardiovascular events is considered necessary. Because EtCO2 is sampled outside the airway, continuous auscultation of breath sounds is recommended as a complementary monitor in this setting. Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov, TRN: NCT04622436, Registration date: 03 November 2020.
